title: The Agentic Information Economy
summary: An internet populated and run by AI agents will need not just reliable data but also a broader information ecology capable of questioning its own inputs and transmitting corrections where they are needed if information changes. But whether this will serve private interests or the public good remains to be seen.

title: Who Owns What AI Learns?
summary: Since frontier AI models have already consumed much of the readily available stock of public knowledge on the internet, what remains is the valuable tacit knowledge embedded within organizations. Whoever sets the terms of how this knowledge is teased out and transferred will set the terms of the next economy.

title: America First Is Jeopardizing Taiwan’s Greatest Asset
summary: Rather than strengthening Taiwan, US demands for market access, technology investment, and defense capabilities are deepening political polarization and eroding the island’s ability to build consensus just when it needs it most. The timing could hardly be worse.

title: When Words Are No Longer for Us
summary: Owing to the proliferation of large language models throughout our software and social systems, we are now undergoing a textpocalypse, marked by not just a deluge of slop but a fundamental unmooring of language and text from lived human experience. The first victim is likely to be the internet itself.

title: Who Will Do the World’s “Most Impossible Job”?
summary: Although the United Nations is facing a financial and political crisis that is almost certain to get worse before it gets better, the field of candidates vying for the organization’s top job is surprisingly crowded. If history is any guide, power politics, more than anything else, will decide the outcome.

title: AI Is Fracking the Open Web
summary: The demand for what digital publishers offer is real and robust, but the old methods of managing it will no longer work when cyberspace is inundated with bots designed to extract value wherever it can be found.
